detail.title: Redundancy and Observer Consensus in Physical Records
detail.summary: Robustness in quantum records emerges not merely from redundancy but from the capacity of the environment to broadcast pointer states effectively. Agreement across observers is conditioned by the alignment of the system-environment interaction and the resilience of these redundant records to local noise. While Quantum Darwinism provides a mechanism for this broadcast, observer agreement requires that information is not only redundant but also locally accessible in a manner that remains invariant across different measurement contexts.
detail.reason: Refining the operational criteria for observer consensus in quantum systems.

detail.title: Redundancy and Observer Consensus in Physical Records
detail.summary: Operationalizing observer consensus requires measuring the redundancy of information stored in the environment. Objective records are those whose pointer states are redundantly accessible to independent observers. The transition to classicality depends on these environmental records resisting noise. Current frameworks provide the necessary metrics, though experimental isolation of these records in noisy environments remains a critical research hurdle.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating refined operational definitions of objective records from peer-reviewed literature.

children.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Record robustness is not merely a static property of environmental state redundancy but depends dynamically on system preparation, local field conditions, and the observer's information structure. External observers rely on relativistic causality, whereas internal observers utilize local observables super-algebras, requiring a self-consistency principle to maintain agreement.
